message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision for this Monopoly turn.

I have $2,966 and a pink monopoly with hotels on all three properties. I am currently on the mortgaged MARVIN_GARDENS. The opponent has only $34 and is in jail. I hold two get-out-of-jail cards.

The opponent owns mostly mortgaged properties with four to three houses on several. Unmortgaging the railroad or Tennessee Avenue would be negative value without a set. Selling the pink hotels would drop rent. The best options are ending the turn, proposing a trade, or holding.

The opponent needs $50 to get out of jail. They can liquidate buildings to cover that cost. My pink hotels are the main threat. I should not trade away cash or a get-out-of-jail card. Selling the hotels would reduce rent and help them survive.

Unmortgaging the railroad would cost $110 without a set. Trading Tennessee Avenue would complete their orange set. I am considering a trade to acquire their dangerous properties, such as Park Place with four houses.

The opponent's Park Place with four houses would cost $1,300 in rent, and Boardwalk with three houses would cost $1,400. Both are within my cash range. The best strategy is to keep the pink hotels and wait for the opponent to land on them.

Jail protects the opponent from my pink hotels. They cannot land on my properties while in jail. I am now considering trading for their dark blues or light blues to eliminate their rent threat. Their desperate cash position may make them willing to trade.

Light blue properties would eliminate another built monopoly. The opponent would not give them away cheaply. Trading Tennessee Avenue would complete their orange set, and those hotels are extremely dangerous. They might want my get-out-of-jail cards to escape jail.

I want the opponent out of jail so they can land on my pink hotels. While in jail, they cannot collect rent from me or move around the board.

Jail is positioned directly before the pink properties. The opponent can land on St. Charles Place immediately upon leaving jail, since that space sits only three spaces ahead of position 10.

Rolling a 3, 4, or 5 from jail lands the opponent directly on St. Charles Place, States Avenue, or Virginia Avenue. That is a 25% chance of hitting a pink hotel immediately upon release. They only have $34 cash, so they must use a get-out-of-jail card to escape.

I will end the turn. Selling houses returns only half their purchase price, so liquidating buildings is costly. I should not trade away cash or a get-out-of-jail card to help them escape.
